audited_plan.image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a rocky substrate. The organism displays eight distinct, overlapping calcareous plates arranged in a linear series along its dorsal surface. The plates are surrounded by a tough, leathery girdle covered in dense, bristle-like spines or setae. The coloration is mottled with shades of grey, brown, and tan, providing camouflage against the rock.
